tools.name: get_vulnerability
tools.description: Get the merged entry for one or more IDs: CVE, GitHub advisory (GHSA), EUVD, or an OSV ID such as PYSEC, GO or RUSTSEC. Returns the description, CVSS, CISA KEV status, EPSS, public exploits, affected packages, fixed versions, priority and source links.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the whole catalog by words: product, vendor, package, CVE ID, common vulnerability name, research metadata or description text. Best match first by default. Each result says which fields matched. When nothing matches, the reply suggests a broader query.

tools.name: get_package
tools.description: Every known vulnerability in one open source package, most urgent first, with the affected ranges and fixed versions published for that package. Give a version to learn which advisories affect it and the lowest upgrade that leaves every affecting range.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Every known vulnerability in one vendor product, such as an operating system, browser, server, CMS or appliance, most urgent first, with the affected versions and fixes. The vendor is optional: with only a product name, a clear match is answered directly and otherwise the candidates are listed. Give

tools.name: list_feed
tools.description: List vulnerabilities newest first (KEV listings by date added when kev is set). Filter by severity, CISA KEV, exploitation, public exploit code, fix availability, ecosystem, vendor, product, text and dates. Use modified_since to pick up changes since a previous run.

tools.name: top_priority
tools.description: What to patch first: the vulnerabilities with the highest priority score (exploitation, EPSS, CVSS, automatability) among those with activity in a time window, optionally narrowed to an ecosystem, vendor or product.

tools.name: check_stack
tools.description: Find known vulnerabilities in what a project or site runs, ranked by what to fix first. Send exact package versions, the raw content of a lockfile (package-lock.json, poetry.lock, go.sum and others), a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM, a Wappalyzer export, or detected technologies such as nginx 1.18.0. findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_feed · Public sink: check_stack · Destructive: list_feed.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_feed · Public sink: check_stack · Destructive: list_feed

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
